rationale: The latest packet is not deployable as-is: the learned sections have grown to ~12.8k characters over 11 reproduction lessons plus 3 submission lessons, with heavy overlap (submit-early guidance restated twice, and one-dimension/near-site steering restated in five places), several lessons parameterized to a single vulnerability family, and a hard stopping condition that makes exact frame-chain and instance correspondence a precondition for accepting a reproduction. That conflicts with the base submission loop's 'prefer another submission over extended analysis' bias and with the packet's own hedge that an earlier fault can itself be the issue. The held-out comparison supports this concern: the latest packet scored 6/10 success with 4 failures versus 7/10 success for the initial packet, and 3 of its failures were runs that never submitted a candidate at all -- the same no-submission mode that dominates the accumulated training failure pool (22 zero-submission failures). The general content is worth keeping, so consolidation rather than rollback is appropriate.
